title: feat(react)!: retire useClientNotifications, a second inbox poller with zero consumers (objectui#7389)
body:
Fixes #7389
Clause-②: yes

Retires `useClientNotifications` from `@object-ui/react`, as ruled on the card (comment 5809224666, letter **remove**). Dispatched under PM claim 5826117848, PM session `session_01BA3nKVUwKQJf8DBxrSVtNC`.

## What changed

- **Deleted** `packages/react/src/hooks/useClientNotifications.ts`: the hook and its two exported types, `UseClientNotificationsOptions` and `UseClientNotificationsResult`. Its private helpers (`toSeverity`, `ClientBearingDataSource`, `hasGetClient`, `useResolvedClient`) had no other reader and go with it. The hook had no tests of its own.
- **Barrel**: its `export *` line leaves `packages/react/src/hooks/index.ts`.
- **Docs**: the "Server-side notifications" section of `content/docs/guide/notifications.md` no longer teaches the hook. It now points at the shell's shared inbox feed (`sharedUserFeeds` in `@object-ui/app-shell`) through the feed's two public surfaces: the header bell in `AppHeader`, and a `global:notifications` page node. It also says the feed itself is not exported, and that a second poller beside the shell is the shape the feed exists to remove.
- **Cadence pin comment**: the header comment of `sharedInboxFeed.cadence-7249.test.tsx` called the hook "the other candidate" with "no call sites". It now records that the hook was retired and is no longer a candidate. Only the comment changes; no assertion does.
- **Doc-example ledger**: `scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs` drops the ledger row keyed on the deleted file's `@example`. If kept, that row reads as STALE and `check:doc-examples` exits 1 (measured below). This path is outside the claim's declared file surface; see "Surface" below.
- **Changeset** `.changeset/7389-retire-use-client-notifications.md`: `minor` on `@object-ui/react` (never `major`, per AGENTS.md section 9). It is marked **BREAKING**, and its migration is: use the shell's shared inbox feed.

## Consumer census (run before deleting, as the ruling requires)

| objectui `ea9d17fb6` (main, re-read before opening this PR) | the same 6 files. None of the touched paths changed since the branch point. | same control, present |
| objectstack `338feda6` (origin/main) | 6 files, all CHANGELOGs or release notes | `SchemaRenderer` found in `.ts`/`.tsx` code |
| hotcrm `087b7c5` (shallow clone, read-only) | 0 | `@object-ui/` imports found |
| cloud | **NOT MEASURED**: not reachable from this session (`git ls-remote` exit 128 on credentials, REST 403) | none |

## Reverse proof: the removal is real at a consumer's resolution path

The probe sits in `packages/components`, where `@object-ui/react` resolves through `node_modules` to the `exports` of `packages/react/package.json` and then to `dist/index.d.ts`. One probe imports the three removed names plus the live control `useSettledSchema`. A second probe imports only controls (`useSettledSchema`, `useNotifications`). Both compile with `tsc --noEmit --strict --ignoreConfig`. Both legs ran from committed state under one lock hold, with an EXIT/INT/TERM trap for the restore:

- **Leg B**: the base source of the two react paths was restored from `e6203d756`. On disk: barrel line count 1, hook file present. React was rebuilt, and `dist/hooks/index.d.ts` then had line count 1. Result: the removed-names probe **exits 0**, and the control probe exits 0.
- **Restore**: `git diff HEAD` is 0 bytes, porcelain is empty, the barrel blob `979a1a0d0` equals HEAD's, and the hook file is absent. Then `dist` was wiped and react rebuilt from HEAD: 0 dist files name the hook (132 emitted files, against 134 in leg B), and the control is present.
- **HEAD leg**: the removed-names probe **exits 2**:
  - `useClientNotifications` gives **TS2724**, "has no exported member named 'useClientNotifications'. Did you mean 'useNotifications'?". The dispatch predicted TS2305. TS2724 reports the same absence; tsc uses that code when it can offer a spelling suggestion.
  - `UseClientNotificationsOptions` and `UseClientNotificationsResult` give **TS2305**.
  - The control probe **exits 0**.
- Runtime: `await import('@object-ui/react')` under plain Node from `packages/components` gives `'useClientNotifications' in m === false`, and `useSettledSchema` and `useNotifications` are functions.

Ledger ablation (why the `check-doc-example-types.mjs` edit is required): the base row was re-inserted through a unique anchor (on disk, 0 rows went to 1). `node scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs` then **exits 1** with `STALE LEDGER ROW packages/react/src/hooks/useClientNotifications.ts useClientNotifications #1`, "no such example in the scan set". After the restore, blob `e96381d17` equals HEAD's and `git diff HEAD` is 0 bytes.

Six entries are **NOT MEASURED**: its provenance leg refused `auth`, `mobile`, `permissions`, `providers`, `react-runtime` and `types` as shared-turbo-cache replays from sibling worktrees. `@object-ui/react` was built by this tree and is among the 28 entries loaded.
- **eslint**, per-rule counts on the touched files, base against head. The base side was read via `git show e6203d756:PATH | eslint --stdin --stdin-filename PATH`. Each `--format json` result held one file, and none was reported as ignored.
  - `hooks/index.ts`, the cadence test and `check-doc-example-types.mjs`: `{}` on both sides.
  - The deleted hook at base: `@typescript-eslint/no-explicit-any` x4 and `react-hooks/set-state-in-effect` x1, all warnings. They leave with the file.
  - Invariance: `eslint.config.js` enables no type-aware linting (no `parserOptions.project` or `projectService`), so this diff cannot move a verdict on an untouched file. Repo-wide `pnpm lint` is left to CI.

## Surface

The claim's file surface did not list `scripts/check-doc-example-types.mjs`. The removal forces its one ledger row out, because the gate goes red on a row whose example is gone (measured above). The script reads the deleted file as text, the kind of reader that item 4 of the dispatch's mechanism list asked to update with the removal. The check is not weakened: the row goes because its subject no longer exists, and the gate's other 88 rows still match.

## Acceptance notes

- Point 4 of triage comment 5548568302 suggested a pin that would let a gate see "a second scheduler over the same ADR-0030 rows". The ruling did not order it, and it is not done here. This PR deletes the only known instance, so a structural guard would be a separate decision. Carrier: none.
